data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, ), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: JunoCam
record.description: JunoCam, a wide-angle visible-light camera for public outreach, was designed to take four-color images with the best spatial resolution to date of Jupiter’s cloud tops. JunoCam is a pushframe imager, similar to the Mars Color Imager on the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter spacecraft. It has a Charge-Coupled Device (CCD) image sensor with a color filter array (CFA) with four spectral bands is bonded to the CCD. The four bands are red (600-800 nanometers), green (500-600 nanometers), blue (420-520 nanometers), and methane absorption (880-900 nanometers). JunoCam, which is fixed to the spacecraft bus, takes a swath of images as the spacecraft rotates. JunoCam has a field of view of 58 degrees and a pixel scale of 0.7 milliradians/pixel. Goals include supporting the Juno Microwave Radiometer (MWR) experiment by unusual atmospheric conditions such as hotspots, searching for convective clouds and lightning in thunderstorms, and deriving the heights of clouds.
